MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 11, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on September 11, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 6, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:11 p.m.)
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Sachs declared a recess and announced that the City Council will
reconvene in the Kershaw Garden (outside city hall) for the invocation and Pledge of Allegiance
as part of the City’s Patriot Day Ceremony.

The City Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. in the Kershaw Garden with all five City Council
Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

City Council Minutes  1  September 11, 2018
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Raths with Boy Scout Troop 1602

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At 6:09 p.m., Mayor Sachs declared a recess and noted that the City Council would return to the
Council Chamber to conduct the regularly-scheduled City Council Meeting.

The City Council reconvened in the Council Chamber at 6:10 p.m. with all five City Council
Members present.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dennis Walsh, Board Member for Saddleback Valley Unified School District, M.V.: urged voters
to look at school board candidates and why they are running before casting their ballot in
November. Mr. Walsh said the School District needs Board Members who want to further the
needs of children, the district, the employees and the City so it’s very important to elect the most
qualified people.

Ryan Farsai, M.V.: stated that he has an ongoing conflict with the City over encroachment issues
on his service station property and he is still seeking a solution.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: noted that today we honor those who lost their lives on September 11, 2005.
She expressed her gratitude to the first responders and discussed the many innocent victims who
perished that day.

Jason Yi, M.V.: announced that he is a senior at Capistrano Valley High School and a member of
the City’s Community of Character Committee. He stated that this month’s character trait is
responsibility and the character movie of the month, The Post, will be shown on Sunday,
September 16, 2018, at 2:00 p.m. in the City Council Chamber.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of August 28, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated August 17, 2018 in the Amount of $4,536,774.34
City Council Minutes  2  September 11, 2018
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated August 24, 2018 in the Amount of $373,473.67

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2018

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2018

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July
  2018

  Received and filed.

7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for July 2018

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

8.  Dissolution of City Council California Voting Rights Act (“CVRA”) Ad Hoc
  Committee and Consideration of Forming a New Voter Education Ad Hoc Committee

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated the City’s CVRA public hearings were part of a corruptive
  process meant to maintain the status-quo. She said that the City Attorney protected the
  Council’s seats for the November election and the Council manipulated the current at-large
  voting process and refused to communicate with the public.

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1) dissolve the
  CVRA Ad Hoc, and (2) form an ad hoc committee to assist in the development of education
  materials for the cumulative voting process. Mayor Sachs appointed Mayor Pro Tem
  Raths and Council Member Kelley to serve on the new Voter Education Ad Hoc
  Committee.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  3  September 11, 2018
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

9.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

10.  Orange County Veterans Advisory Council

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

11.  June 30, 2017 Pension Valuation and Unfunded Liabilities Update

  Mayor Sachs congratulated his colleagues on the work they have done to address the City’s
  unfunded liability.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report. She announced
  that Mission Viejo has seen a $1.7 million decline in its unfunded liability and is currently
  funded at 80%, the highest it has been since before the recession.

  By consensus, the City Council received the report.

12.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update from Chief Vuong

  Deputy Wayne Dixon presented statistics from 2012-2017 traffic surveys. He noted a
  157% average increase in traffic on the city's roadways from 2017-2018. Deputy Dixon
  also outlined the increase in traffic citations that have been issued and noted that Mission
  Viejo has the lowest fatal traffic collision rate to percentage of population when compared
  to 14 other OCSD contract cities.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

City Council Minutes  4  September 11, 2018
 Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum thanked Council Member Kelley for providing the Southern California
Association of Governments (SCAG) report and she expressed her gratitude to staff for the solemn
9/11 service earlier in the evening. She also wished her son Spencer a happy 20th birthday.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that the next Olympic Promotion Committee meeting will
be held tomorrow.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley complimented Supervisor Lisa Bartlett and her staff for their Veterans
Resource Fair at Saddleback College on September 4, 2018. She said it was very well attended
and she was impressed with the number of booths and the amount of information that was
available. The City had a very good presence with two booths and offered a variety of resources
for veterans. Council Member Kelley also complimented Mission Viejo Library staff for the many
programs they offer, including a Veteran’s Resource Center in the library. She announced that the
Marine Adoption Committee has planned its annual golf tournament on October 12 this year and,
in addition to playing golf, there are opportunities to support the Marines with a golf ball drop
fundraiser. Residents can purchase golf balls by mailing a check to the Marine Adoption
Committee, paying in person at the Murray Community Center, or online at
http://www.teeitupforemarines.com. In closing, Council Member Kelley thanked student Jason Yi
for coming to the meeting to speak about the character quality of the month which is responsibility.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked City staff for putting together tonight's Patriot Day event and he
thanked Boy Scout Troop 1602 for assisting him in the Pledge of Allegiance. On this Patriot Day,
he also expressed his gratitude to the Orange County Sheriff’s deputies and the Orange County
Fire Authority firefighters for all that they do to protect the City.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs stated that comments made by a member of the public on agenda item 8 were wrong
in every capacity. He announced that as the founder of Secure OC Schools, he had the opportunity
to attend a lockdown drill at a local school recently. Personnel on the campus where the drill took
place were as trained as any and yet there were failings which could have caused some causalities.
He admonished parents to not take “yes” for an answer but rather engage with and put pressure on
the schools regarding safety measures. He stated that the lockdown drill was a real eye-opener to
observe and he stressed that Secure OC Schools is there to help identify gaps that may exist in the
schools and help close those gaps either through legislation or funding. Mayor Sachs announced
that he had the honor of speaking at the Orange County Fire Authority Patriot Day Memorial
earlier in the day and he read the first paragraph from the speech he gave. He noted that the purpose
was, of course, to honor those who gave the ultimate sacrifice but also to pay respect to all those
who, after seeing the events of 9/11, still choose to join the fire or police department today. Those

 individuals know that their next call could result in a major impact to themselves or their families,
yet they still step up. Mayor Sachs said it is important to understand that without a draft, the
military in the United States is 100% volunteer and the men and women in the armed forces and
public safety make this a wonderful country indeed.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:43 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 25, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  6  September 11, 2018
